title: How to build your slides
note: Silent screen tour with captions now; Opti voices these lines later (one take each), then the tour is re-timed to the real clip lengths.

yell.text: Winters are long and cold. Snow can stay for months, so bison dig through it to find grass.
Bison, elk, and gray wolves live here. Bison have thick fur, and wolves hunt in packs.
Energy goes from grasses to elk to gray wolves.
Lake trout don't belong in Yellowstone Lake. They eat the cutthroat trout that bears and eagles need.
In 1995, people brought gray wolves back to Yellowstone, so the food web is more complete.

lines.say: Have you ever made a presentation? Here's how to build yours in the Park Slide Studio.
A presentation is a few slides you show while you talk. Each slide has one big idea, one picture, and a few words.
Look at these two slides. The first one is short, with a real photo and a fact. The second one has too many words for a visitor.
Press Got it, then pick your park.
Your six slides are up here, one for each criterion.
Need facts? Each slide has Field Notes with true facts about your park. Pick one, and write it in your own words.
Start with slide one. Not sure how to begin? Press Use a sentence starter, then finish the sentence.
act: TYPE:#st-text:geysers, hot springs, and wild animals.

lines.say: Watch the word counter. Keep each slide between five and thirty words.
Now pick a real photo. Tap one, and it jumps onto your slide.
These three checks turn green when your slide is strong: the right number of words, a picture, and a specific detail.
Want your visitor to hear you? Press Record my voice, talk, then press Stop. Your voice goes inside your slides.
On the food web slide, pick a plant, an animal that eats it, and an animal that eats that one.
When every circle at the top is lit, your slides meet all six criteria.
Press Present to practice out loud. You have two minutes, so talk about each slide for about twenty seconds.
Last, press Make my video. Your slides and your voice turn into a video. Upload it to Canvas. You did it, presenter!
